mentl/8f0a25c:
Closes Ω.4. The parser's 13 acc ++ [X] iterative-builder sites
now use the buffer-counter substrate pattern: allocate a buffer at
loop entry, thread (buf, count) through tail-recursion via
push_node, slice at the end. Same pattern as Ω.3's lex_from
push_tok.

Sites converted (recursive parse loops):

• parse_program / parse_stmt_list — top-level statement list
• parse_fn_params / parse_params_tail — function parameter list
• parse_paren_or_tuple / parse_tuple_tail — tuple expression elements
• parse_list_literal / parse_list_elems — list expression elements
• parse_block_expr / parse_block_body — block statements + final expr
• parse_match / parse_match_arms — match expression arms
• parse_lambda / parse_lambda_params — lambda parameter list
• parse_type_ty / parse_type_ty_tail — tuple-type element list

push_node helper (the parser's analog of lex_from's push_tok):
  fn push_node(buf, count, node) = {
    let extended = list_extend_to(buf, count + 1)
    let written  = list_set(extended, count, node)
    (written, count + 1)
  }

Each parse loop's signature changes:
  Before: parse_X(tokens, pos, acc) -> (List, Int)
  After:  parse_X(tokens, pos, buf, count) -> (buf, count, Int)
  Caller wraps: allocate buf, call loop, slice(final_buf, 0, final_count)

Cross-codebase D-class drift status post-Ω.4:

• D1 (acc ++ [X]): zero sites in parser. Lexer (Ω.3), lower
  collect_top_level_names (Ω.3), backends collect_top_level_fn_names
  (Ω.3), parser (this commit) — all iterative builders converted.
  Remaining sites are bounded-N single-shot constructions
  (lower.ka:205 LBlock final, wasm.ka:201/308 collect-strings,
  flagged for natural γ-phase touches).
• D2 (str_eq == 1): zero sites across the entire project.
• D3 (string-dispatch if-else for token kinds): zero sites
  across the project.

The parser is now substrate-coherent at every layer:
  - typed Token dispatch (no string equality)
  - buffer-counter iterative builders (no O(N²) allocation)
  - exhaustive variant m

mentl/8f35a8d:
The rewrite machinery (build_rewrite_map, apply_rewrite, find_rewrite effect) existed but was never called from lower_expr's Call dispatch. Effect op calls like bump() and count() fell through to dummy function calls instead of being inlined as state updates + resume values.

Now lower_expr checks find_rewrite(name) before the generic call path. Handler arms are inlined directly: bump() becomes {n = n+1; ()} and count() becomes n. bind_rewrite_params handles ops with parameters. All 7 WASM crucibles pass on wasmtime including handler state (counter) and simultaneous state updates (ultimate fib).
noodles/8f7aa47:
The builder heard hard clipping, melody-forward. The chain audit showed
the D7 ceiling running its 13-19% third-harmonic zone at ordinary
program level, and the live/export A/B found why: D15's input-comp
bypass is level-neutral only at the calibration level. A bypassed
compressor is not a static gain, and on sustained content the missing
squeeze left the live stems 2-3 dB hotter than the export renders of
the same material (harmony -13.5 vs -16.6 rms). The ceiling crunched
nearly continuously, and D17's presence shelf lifted exactly the band
where midrange third harmonics land, so the clearer mix unmasked it.
The carve itself measured level-neutral (master delta 0.2 dB), the
stacks +0.6 dB, the depth floor ~0, and the voice trim was cleared
first: Tone only pools a voice on envelope silence, so trims never cut
a ringing tail.

Fix inside D15's rules: measured per-track trims at the bypass point
(harmony -3.1, bass -2.6, melody -1.9 dB), restoring live-to-export
parity where it matters. After: live stems within ~1 dB of export,
master drive into the ceiling down 1.1 dB, stable under wet floor plus
ninth stacks. Peaks stay less controlled than export - that is D15's
standing trade, and restoring the comps live is the named fuller fix if
the crunch still bites.
